summary: Feed s083_single to IDS is degraded: 8.6% TCP packet loss (186/2165 packets) exceeds 1% threshold. All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, one-way, oversize, truncation, tunnels, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream capture loss before the IDS - most commonly SPAN/mirror port oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion under burst load. SPAN ports drop packets when switch CPU/buffers are busy and have no lossless buffering, creating gaps in the TCP sequence seen at the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions and full payload for stream reassembly and signature matching. With 8.6% missing TCP segments, the IDS cannot reliably reassemble flows, misses exploits split across missing packets, generates incomplete alerts and false negatives, and loses detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN/mirror with passive TAP (and ensure packet broker has adequate buffering) to provide lossless, line-rate copy to the 1 Gbps IDS port. If TAP already in use, add broker-level buffering/QoS and filter irrelevant traffic to prevent broker drops.
